30.0.0.en: The altar of incense is placed in the middle of the Holy Place, before the Holy of Holies. It is different from the bronze altar, which stands before the door of the tabernacle of meeting in the outer court. It is made of durable acacia wood that does not rot and is overlaid with plates of gold (v. 38). As we said concerning the Ark of the Covenant, the wood signifies the humanity of Christ and the gold His divinity; the wood also signifies the Virgin, while the gold signifies Christ who was born of her womb (Figure 18). Figure (18:) The altar of incense

30.1.0.en: The dimensions of the altar of incense are a cubit in length and a cubit in breadth, that is, square, and its height is two cubits. It has four horns, which are part of the corner post and not horns attached to it, to declare that the altar's strength comes from itself. It signifies the mighty Christ, who offered Himself up on the Cross as an atoning sacrifice for us, like the fragrance of incense with which God is pleased with man.

30.2.0.en: The top of the altar, all its sides and its horns are covered with gold, that is, the divinity was united with the humanity perfectly in Christ. A crown, that is, a raised border, is made for it around its upper surface, as a beautiful sight and to protect the incense and the coals from falling to the ground.

30.3.0.en: Two gold rings are made, joined and united to the altar on its two sides, so that a pole of acacia wood overlaid with gold may be put through each of them to carry it. The altar of incense is placed in the middle of the Holy Place before the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies; on its right is the table of showbread and on its left the golden lampstand.

30.4.0.en: Aaron: all the priests are meant.

30.4.1.en: He dresses the lamps: he prepares them and makes them ready.

30.4.2.en: He lights the lamps: that is, he kindles them.

30.4.3.en: The priests place the incense every morning and every evening when they change the oil and replenish it in the lampstand so that it gives light morning and evening. In the same way, they offer a burnt offering on the bronze altar morning and evening. All these declare that Christ offers for us a complete and continual redemption that rises as a sweet fragrance before God, so that He is pleased with us. He is the light of the world, and He works always in the believers by His Holy Spirit, like the continual incense and the lampstand that shines always in the Holy Place.

30.5.0.en: He warns against three things concerning the altar of incense, which are:

30.5.1.en: 1- Offering strange incense other than the composition that God told Moses about, which will be mentioned in this same chapter (v. 34). This is a declaration that Christ alone, whom the incense signifies, is the Redeemer.

30.5.2.en: 2- No sacrifice or offering is to be offered on it, because these are offered on the bronze altar, whereas this altar is set apart for incense only.

30.5.3.en: 3- No wine or oil is to be poured on it, as is done on the bronze altar.

30.5.4.en: For the same purpose, namely that this altar is set apart for incense, the rite here declares one aspect of the Cross, which is the incense that signifies Christ, who pleased the Father by the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross like the fragrance of incense.

30.6.0.en: Most holy to the Lord: it is set apart for the service of God and cannot be used for any other purpose.

30.6.1.en: Aaron puts the blood on it once every year on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16:18, 19) before he enters the Holy of Holies with the incense. This confirms that the incense is a symbol of Christ who was slain for us on the Cross. The blood is an atonement for the sins of the priest and the people, and so the blood is mingled with the incense on the altar of incense, because the two are symbols of the one sacrifice of Christ.

30.6.2.en: May you be like Christ, so that you are a sweet fragrance before God through your thoughts, your words and your deeds. Rather, be distinct from the rest of the world, as a child of God who has the fragrance of Christ, and do not resemble the people of the world in their faults.

30.7.0.en: God commanded that the people be numbered and that a ransom be paid for each one of the males. Every man twenty years old and above pays an amount of silver to redeem his soul, and this is for the following reasons:

30.7.1.en: 1- A declaration of every person's need of the redemption of Christ, who is the Word of God and is signified by the silver.

30.7.2.en: 2- Thanksgiving to God, who redeemed the firstborn of the children of Israel, and the destroying angel did not kill them in Egypt. This signifies responding to the love of Christ the Redeemer, who gave Himself on the Cross for His children, so we give Him our money, that is, the silver.

30.7.3.en: God warned against neglecting the numbering and the payment of the ransom, lest a plague come upon them as happened in the days of David. God's anger against David was because of his numbering of the people, for:

30.7.4.en: 1- God had not commanded him to make this numbering.

30.7.5.en: 2- David tried to boast of their number, that is, he fell into the sin of pride (2 Sam 24:10-17).

30.8.0.en: Twenty years old: the completion of maturity and the age of majority. Whoever reaches this age joins the army to fight (Num 1:3). The tribe of Levi was exempted from paying the ransom because they are consecrated to the service of the Lord (Num 1:

30.8.1.en: 47-53.(Everyone who passes over to those who are numbered: that is, everyone who has reached the age of twenty and above and has passed under the counting. The shekel of the sanctuary: the priests kept accurate scales in the Temple, so it was called the shekel of the sanctuary, that is, a shekel that is exact and precise, more than the ordinary shekel, and it is about 12 grams of silver.

30.8.2.en: Gerah: that is, a grain, because it weighs a carob seed, and it equals 1/20 of the shekel of the sanctuary, that is, about 0.6 grams.

30.8.3.en: Every man offered half a shekel, that is, about 6 grams (some say 8 or 9 grams), which in any case is an amount of silver that both the poor and the rich can pay, since every soul has the same value before God, whether the person is rich or poor. It is a symbol of man's response to God's love and his appreciation of redemption. Christ paid the tax of the two drachmas, which is the ransom (Mt 17:24-27).

30.9.0.en: This silver is used in the building materials of the tabernacle of meeting, that is, for the bases of the pillars and the hooks. The silver signifies Christ the Redeemer, for redemption is the foundation of the spiritual building.

30.9.1.en: Remember the love of Christ the Redeemer and His care for you, so that you may respond to it, not only by giving the firstfruits and the tithes, but by serving God and laying down your life for His sake.

30.10.0.en: The laver is a wide vessel, most likely circular in shape, with a base on which it rests. It is made of bronze, which signifies steadfastness and strength, and water is put in it, and it is placed between the bronze altar and the Holy Place. It signifies Baptism, by which we are born again and are established in the life with God. It is circular because it signifies the salvation offered to the whole world, and no measurements were specified for it, so that it might declare salvation to everyone who believes in Christ (Figure 19). Figure (19:) The laver

30.11.0.en: The priests wash in this laver before they come forward to serve, as a declaration of the importance of purity before entering the service of God, and as a symbol of Baptism, the entrance to the spiritual life. The laver is placed between the bronze altar and the Holy Place, but washing in it is required before entering any service, whether at the bronze altar or in the Holy Place. It was placed before the Holy Place because those who wash in it are the priests only, who alone enter the Holy Place.

30.11.1.en: The washing of the hands is a sign of the purity of deeds, and the washing of the feet a sign of the purity of conduct.

30.12.0.en: Washing was necessary, otherwise the priest would die if he entered without washing, since this would be considered contempt for God's commands and His dwelling place. Washing is a symbol of the purity that Christ the Redeemer gives us.

30.12.1.en: Take care of the purity of your mind and its cleansing, and of casting all your troubles on God, before any spiritual work such as prayer at home, the Divine Liturgy, or reading the Holy Bible, by reading a psalm, making prostrations (metanoias), or repeating a hymn....

30.13.1.en: Spices of fragrance: that is, a perfumed or sweetened perfume.

30.13.2.en: 1- Pure myrrh (liquid myrrh): a gum that flows from one of the thorny trees and falls from it in drops, so it is called liquid myrrh, and it is the purest kind of myrrh since it has no impurities.

30.13.3.en: 2- Sweet cinnamon: the inner bark of the cinnamon tree, which has a well-known sweet fragrance in addition to its pleasant taste.

30.13.4.en: 3- Sweet calamus: a kind of reed that has a sweet fragrance.

30.13.5.en: 4- Cassia: the bark of one of the trees, which has a sweet fragrance. Some say it is the outer bark of the cinnamon tree, though it may be another tree. It is called cassia (salikha) because the outer bark is stripped (tuslakh) from the trees.

30.13.6.en: God specified the quantities of these materials to be mixed together, with a hin of olive oil added to them, which is about 4 liters. These quantities come in the end to about 18 kilograms. Thus the anointing oil is formed with a sweet fragrance, and with it the kings, priests and prophets are anointed. It signifies the Sacrament of the Holy Myron.

30.14.0.en: He commanded him to anoint all the parts of the tabernacle of meeting, so that they would be dedicated, or sanctified, or consecrated to God, and a blessing to everyone who touches them, and not be used for anything except worship.

30.15.0.en: This anointing is used to anoint the priests, as has passed in (ch. 29).

30.16.0.en: This oil differs from all the perfumed oils that people use to give a fragrance to their bodies, and even if they use the same materials, they would be in different quantities. But whoever disobeys the word of God and makes the same exactly, to perfume his own body or the body of any person who is a stranger to the children of Israel, that person is set apart and cut off, that is, he does not become a member in the congregation of God.

30.16.1.en: May you have the virtues that adorn your life, and likewise holy worship and self-sacrificing service, so that your fragrance may be sweet before God, like the anointing oil, which is the work of the Holy Spirit.

30.17.0.en: The Lord gave Moses the ingredients of the composition of the incense, which are:-

30.17.1.en: 1- Stacte: the gum of the storax tree.

30.17.2.en: 2- Onycha: the shells of a water creature called the "winged-shell mollusk," which has a sweet fragrance when burned.

30.17.3.en: 3- Galbanum: one of the fragrant gums.

30.17.4.en: 4- Frankincense: a gum from thorny trees.

30.17.5.en: All these materials are mixed in equal quantities, and they give a sweet fragrance when burned.

30.18.0.en: These materials are mixed with salt and become holy incense, that is, set apart for the worship of God.

30.19.0.en: The preceding materials are beaten small, and they become the holy incense, which is placed in a golden vessel beside the altar of incense, before the Holy of Holies.

30.20.0.en: This incense, with the preceding quantities, is set apart for the worship of God, and no one may make the like of it to enjoy its fragrance in his house, out of honor and sanctification of this incense. Whoever makes the like of it is cut off from the people of God, that is, he is cast out and loses his membership.

30.20.1.en: The Church in the New Testament uses incense for the following reasons:

30.20.2.en: 1- It was and still is offered as honor to God. God commanded it to Moses in the Old Testament, and its idea remains firm in the New Testament.

30.20.3.en: 2- Offering feelings of love for God, like the sinful woman in the house of Simon (Lk 7:36-50) and like David in his prayers (Ps 141:2).

30.20.4.en: 3- It signifies Christ the Redeemer, who offered His life for us on the Cross, and His good Father smelled a sweet fragrance on Golgotha.

30.20.5.en: 4- It signifies the prayers of the saints and of all the believers, with which God rejoices, as the Book of Revelation declares (Rev 5:8, 8:3, 4).

30.20.6.en: 5- Just as incense rises toward heaven as a sweet fragrance, so the life of the believers should rise with their virtues as a sweet fragrance toward heaven.

30.20.7.en: For your fragrance to be sweet before God, your life must be mixed with many virtues, and you must crush yourself with the sorrows of toil and spiritual striving, so that your heart and your life become holy to Christ.

30.20.8.en: The makers of the tabernacle of meeting and the sanctification of the Sabbath

31.0.s.en: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

31.0.0.en: Bezaleel: his name means in the shadow or protection of God. He was the grandson of Hur, who supported the hand of Moses when he was praying at the time of the war with Amalek (ch. 17:10). Because of the greatness of the house of God, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, after He had specified to Moses everything in the tabernacle, its measurements and its design, He also supported it by choosing the one responsible for making the tabernacle. He chose a Jewish man named Bezaleel from the tribe of Judah, from which Christ, the leader of the journey of our salvation, came, and made him the chief of the craftsmen for the work of the house of God. The following is noted in his selection:

31.0.1.en: 1- The most important arrangement for completing the service is the servant himself, so God took care in choosing Bezaleel to lead the work.

31.0.2.en: 2- God chose him because he knew many crafts, which he had learned in Egypt, advanced in the arts at that time, and then filled him with understanding and knowledge by His Holy Spirit. Thus the grace of God is mingled with human knowledge, whose source is also God.

31.0.3.en: 3- He knows many trades; he is an artist and is able to lead the craftsmen in the various crafts, even if some of them are more skilled than he in a particular craft, yet he is able to lead them. The leader organizes the work and leads it even if some of his followers are more gifted than he in a certain part of the work.

31.0.4.en: Care for the leader of every ministry and support him spiritually, emotionally and materially so that he may lead the work. Pray that God will send him, and be careful in your choice of him. And if you are a leader, take care for the purity of your heart and trust in God in everything, so that He may do His work.

31.1.0.en: Aholiab: the meaning of his name is tent of the father. God chose him from the tribe of Dan, which is the least of the tribes in standing, because God loves everyone and chooses His servants from every place. Just as He chose Bezaleel from the tribe of Judah, from which Christ came, He chose Aholiab from a tribe of lesser rank.

31.1.1.en: To complete the service, God commanded Moses to appoint a helper for Bezaleel, namely Aholiab, and likewise to call all the artists in the various crafts to take part in this great work, to confirm the importance of cooperation and participation in work within the Church.

31.2.0.en: He did not forget anything inside the tabernacle of meeting, whether the furniture or the materials used, for everything has value in the house of God and must be cared for because it is in the house of God.

31.3.0.en: At the end of God's talk with Moses on the mountain, He returns to confirm the importance of keeping the Sabbath. The following is noted in this commandment:

31.3.1.en: 1- He calls them "My Sabbaths," for the people of God sanctify the seventh day for the sake of God, His worship and His love.

31.3.2.en: 2- Keeping the day of God every week is a sign of our sonship to God. By this we differ from the rest of mankind, who do not care to set apart a day for God. It is like a covenant between God and His people throughout all the days.

31.3.3.en: 3- He repeats it after the command to make the tabernacle of meeting, lest the workers think that it is permitted to work on erecting the tabernacle on the Sabbath days. It was required to devote oneself to worship only on this day.

31.3.4.en: If the glory of Sunday has surpassed the glory of the Sabbath because of the Resurrection of Christ, the Sabbath signifies rest not only in the completion of the creation of the world, but it signifies Sunday, on which Christ completed our redemption and proclaimed our salvation. Therefore may you take care to sanctify Sunday and give yourself a greater opportunity on it to enjoy the worship of God and His service, so that you experience His work in you more deeply.

31.4.1.en: God completes His commandments of the law of the Sabbath, saying:

31.4.2.en: 4- The penalty for breaking the Sabbath by doing material works on it was severe, namely death, because the Sabbath signifies the devotion of the heart to God. Whoever lets the love of the world into his heart profanes it and has no life with Christ. This is the first time the penalty for breaking the Sabbath is mentioned, as it is mentioned in (Num 15:

31.5.0.en: God rested and was refreshed: what is meant is God's satisfaction with His work, for God does not grow weary or breathe as human beings do, but He speaks in expressions that human beings understand, to teach them that rest is a spiritual rest, by being with God.

31.5.1.en: God adds in the law of the Sabbath:

31.5.2.en: 5- The necessity of holding fast to it throughout their lives and in all generations, that is, their children. Even now the Sabbath day has respect in the Church, but the glory of Sunday has surpassed it, so the Church celebrates Sunday and also the Sabbath of every week, and does not fast strictly on them nor make prostrations (metanoias), because they are days of joy. Here He stresses the importance of continuing to keep the Sabbath, that is, carrying out God's commandments throughout life.
